channel.title: JustinCredible Tech
channel.description: Phones, computers, apps, gadgets and the companies behind them.

item.title: FAA Issues a Nationwide Ground Stop After a Communication Issue at Air Traffic Control Centers
item.description: On Friday afternoon, November 13, 2026, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop on departing flights after a communication issue affecting Air Route Traffic Control Centers. The notice was later taken down from the FAA website; as of 3:32 p.m. Central time, the agency's live status board no longer listed a nationwide stop, though delays continued at some airports.

item.title: Google and Samsung's Gemini Glasses Open for Preorder at $395, Shipping December 10
item.description: Google opened preorders on November 12, 2026, for Intelligent Eyewear built with Samsung, Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. The audio-and-camera glasses start at $395 and go on sale in stores and online on December 10.

item.title: Update: Microsoft 365 Outage Enters a Second Day as Recovery Begins
item.description: The Microsoft 365 and Outlook outage that started at 10:17 a.m. Central Time on November 12, 2026, continued overnight and into Friday. Microsoft says recovery is underway, with broader improvements in North America, and has extended the email timeout window to 48 hours. The incident is still not fully resolved.

item.title: Update: Nvidia Edges Higher in Premarket After Huang Resignation
item.description: One day after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO, the stock closed Thursday down 4.3% at $166.19 after falling as much as about 14%. In Friday premarket trading it was about 1.6% to 1.7% higher as of about 7:15 a.m. Central Time. Interim CEO Colette Kress takes the first big test on Tuesday, when Nvidia still plans to report earnings.

item.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress Named Interim Chief
item.description: Nvidia announced on November 12, 2026 that founder Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, after a week of reports about two extramarital affairs. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, the stock fell as much as about 14%, and President Trump says Tim Cook should get the job.

item.title: Microsoft 365 and Outlook Outage Is Ongoing, Hitting Teams, SharePoint, and Copilot Worldwide
item.description: A widespread Microsoft 365 outage that started around 10:17 a.m. Central Time on November 12, 2026, is still ongoing. Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Copilot, and Defender XDR are affected. Microsoft says servers unexpectedly went offline, not a traffic surge.

item.title: Nvidia's Board Is Reportedly Preparing to Oust Jensen Huang After a Second Alleged Affair
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reports Nvidia's board is preparing to remove founder and CEO Jensen Huang and was set to meet as soon as November 11, 2026, after The New York Times reported a second alleged affair, this time with an executive who reports to him. Shares fell more than 7% after hours.

item.title: GTA 6 Will Stream on Xbox One at Launch, and Rockstar Confirms a 30fps Target on Every Console
item.description: Rockstar and Microsoft confirmed on November 10, 2026 that Grand Theft Auto VI will be playable on Xbox One through Xbox Cloud Gaming starting November 19, using Xbox Series S graphics settings. Rockstar also confirmed a 30fps target on PS5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

item.title: Nvidia Stock Falls as Much as 8% After the Board Opens a Probe Tied to Jensen Huang's Affair
item.description: Nvidia shares slid as much as 8% at Monday's open, erasing more than $280 billion in value, after the board opened an independent investigation tied to CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The New York Times also reports a Commerce Department probe of her company, Megaspeed, was moved to the Justice Department after Nvidia's general counsel reached out.

item.title: Nvidia's Board Opens an Investigation After Jensen Huang Admits an Affair With a Suspected Chinese Spy
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told employees he was unfaithful to his wife, and Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation into reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The board says it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised, and Huang stays CEO.

item.title: Your iPhone Keyboard Has a Hidden List of About 100,000 Phrases It Won't Suggest
item.description: A researcher found an undisclosed list inside iOS of roughly 100,000 words and phrases that the iPhone keyboard won't autocomplete or, in most cases, swipe-type. Most are slurs, sex and drug terms, but political phrases from both sides are on it too. You can still type all of them letter by letter.

item.title: LEGO's First Official Godzilla Set Has 5,363 Pieces and Stands 27.5 Inches Tall
item.description: LEGO revealed LEGO Ideas Godzilla (21375) on Godzilla Day: a fan-designed, 5,363-piece build that's the biggest LEGO Ideas set ever. It goes on sale November 27, 2026, for $449.99.

item.title: Roku Is Retiring Its Aquatic Life Fish Tank Screensaver on Dec. 1
item.description: Roku is showing users an on-screen notice that its Aquatic Life aquarium screensaver will no longer be available starting December 1, 2026, and that affected screens will switch to Roku City. Here's the backstory and how to pick something else.

item.title: Meta Reportedly Built a Humanoid Robot Prototype Called Max in Three Months
item.description: According to The Information, Meta and Chinese robot maker Fourier built a roughly 106-pound humanoid prototype named Max, and a Max 2 is already underway. Meta says it's for internal research, not for sale.

item.title: Hackers Drained About $6.3 Billion From Binance in the Largest Crypto Theft on Record
item.description: Most of the money left Binance's hot wallets in about 20 minutes on October 29. Binance says a hacked engineer's laptop may have been the way in, blockchain analysts point to North Korea, and about $3 billion has been frozen so far.

item.title: Alphabet Sheds Over $500 Billion in a Day as AI Search Earns Google Less: What It Means for You
item.description: Alphabet stock fell more than 12% on October 29 after Q3 results showed slower search ad growth, lower ad revenue from AI Mode searches and negative free cash flow from heavy AI spending. Google's answer: more ads inside AI Overviews and AI Mode.

item.title: DoorDash Agrees to Buy Instacart for About $17 Billion: What It Could Mean for Your Delivery Apps
item.description: DoorDash has agreed to acquire Instacart in a roughly $17 billion deal. Members would eventually pay one fee instead of two, but regulators still have to sign off and closing isn't expected until late 2027 or the first half of 2028.

item.title: Apple Unveils Its First Touchscreen Mac: What the New MacBook Pro Means for You
item.description: Apple's new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is the first Mac you can touch. Here's how touch works, what it costs, and who should care.

item.title: Apple Announces the M6 14-Inch MacBook Pro and iMac. Pre-Orders Open October 28
item.description: Apple put its new M6 chip in the 14-inch MacBook Pro ($1,999) and the 24-inch iMac ($1,499). Same designs, faster chips, and a rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro could be right behind them.

item.title: Some Public Discord Server Messages May Soon Show Up in Google Search
item.description: Starting in mid-December, messages from public channels in Discord's Discoverable Servers can appear in web search if server admins allow it. DMs, group chats and private servers aren't included, and you can opt out.

item.title: Microsoft Is Offering Voluntary Buyouts to About 60,000 Employees: What It Means
item.description: Microsoft's new Voluntary Exit Offer covers roughly 27% of its workforce. Here's who's eligible, what's different from a layoff, and why the timing matters.

item.title: Some iPhone Duo Owners Report Cracked Inner Screens Days After Launch
item.description: A small number of early iPhone Duo owners say their inner screens cracked along the hinge within hours or days. How widespread it is remains unclear, and Apple hasn't commented.

item.title: Apple's First Foldable iPhone Is in Stores, Starting at $1,999
item.description: iPhone Duo went on sale October 23 with a 7.6-inch folding screen, a 5.4-inch outer display and Touch ID in the side button. Supply is tight, and early reviews love the hinge but question the small cover screen.

item.title: Apple Says iPhone Duo Is ‘Like Two Products’ — So… Would You Pay $1,999?
item.description: A day after the unveil, Apple executives defended the iPhone Duo’s $1,999 sticker, the foldable display, and the secrecy. Preorders Oct 16, ships Oct 23.

item.title: Apple’s iPhone Duo is real — foldable, $1,999, ships October 23
item.description: Apple unveiled its first foldable iPhone on September 9, 2026. Here’s the price, ship date, and how it sits next to iPhone 18 Pro.
